model: Distributable earnings to ordinary shareholders capitalised at cost of equity (FCFE payout-capacity, engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: ~10yr average of the base revenue path (guided -7.5% FY2026, trough FY2027-28, ~2-3% nominal thereafter). Equity CAGR rejected as the primary rate -- see warning.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+7.8% 5yr) diverges by >30% from revenue (+2.3% 5yr, -1.8% 3yr) and EPS (-2.5% 5yr, -10.9% 3yr). Book value has compounded on retained earnings that were reinvested in receivables, contract assets and PPP concessions while the market prices that book at ~0.23x (RMB12.97 ordinary BVPS vs ~RMB2.74 H price) -- book growth is not evidence of value growth here.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs undefined: OCF less gross capex negative in FY2018, FY2020-FY2025 (FY2025 -RMB31.5bn). SBC immaterial, so there is no SBC-adjusted vs reported FCF gap. H1 FY2026 net profit attributable -26.8% YoY on revenue -7.7%.

scenario_narratives.base: Trough then nominal-GDP growth. FY2026 revenue on guidance (RMB1,011.8bn, -7.5%), a further -3% in FY2027, flat FY2028, then 2-3% on 15th Five-Year Plan rail/water spend and overseas contracts. Ordinary-shareholder NI margin 1.63% -> 2.0% (below the 2.3-2.6% FY2019-24 band). Payout capacity 32% -> 60% as the new PPP mechanism shrinks concession spend and the debt-swap programme stops receivable growth. The axes are local-government payment behaviour and PPP taper, not volume.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fiscal arrears are cleared by the special-bond and debt-swap programmes; receivable days normalise; overseas (+16.5% new contracts FY2025) and mining lift mix. Revenue flat in FY2027 and 3-4% thereafter; margin back to 2.4%; payout capacity 70% -- the level clean-surplus retention implies at ~6.6% ROE and 2.5% growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: The receivables build (+35% FY2025, 139 days) turns into impairments, property losses deepen, and price competition defeats the anti-involution campaign. Revenue falls through FY2029 (cumulative ~-18% from FY2025), margin ~1.2-1.3%, and only ~30% of earnings is distributable for three years. Equity survives -- central-SOE status makes a wipe-out remote -- but it compounds nothing.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CREC is valued on what ordinary shareholders can actually be paid, not on enterprise free cash flow. The group's unlevered FCF has been negative 7 of 9 years because it funds its local-government customers through receivables and builds PPP concessions on its own balance sheet; ordinary equity is a thin geared claim behind RMB465bn net debt, RMB170bn NCI and RMB55bn perpetual notes. Earnings attributable to ordinary shareholders are already after all those claims, so they are capitalised at a 10.5% RMB cost of equity with net debt held at zero, after a payout-capacity haircut that charges the cash-conversion problem explicitly: only 30% of earnings is paid today, rising to 60% in the base case. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon (12x at 10.5%/2%) and a 10x cap on the distributable flow (~6x earnings), which binds in all three scenarios -- a deliberate no-re-rate stance for a stock whose P/E has sat ~3-7x for a decade and which trades at ~0.23x book.
valuation_philosophy.fcf_normalization: Rejected for the headline (see inputs.fcf_normalization_note): normalising a series that is negative 7 of 9 years requires assuming the PPP taper and receivable reversal the model is trying to test, and the resulting equity value swings by more than the market cap per 1pp of margin.
valuation_philosophy.terminal_value_approach: max(0, min(Gordon at CoE, 10x terminal distributable flow)); cap binds in every scenario. 10x a 60%-payout flow is ~6x earnings, inside CREC's own historical P/E range, so no multiple expansion is assumed.
key_risks_to_valuation: Receivables (RMB485.9bn, +35% YoY) are impaired at scale -- book value and future NI both overstated; this is the bear case and a plausible tail beyond it.
PPP/concession spend does not taper (it rose to RMB42.0bn in FY2025), keeping payout capacity near 30%.
Property segment losses widen with the China housing downturn.
Rising gearing (78.1%) or a funding-cost spike squeezes the post-interest margin -- 61% of borrowings are floating.
SASAC-directed capital allocation (strategic projects, NCI raises, perpetual issuance) dilutes ordinary-shareholder economics.
The H-share class persistently trades ~35-40% below the A-share class; the RMB value per share is the same for both, so an H-share holder may never see the gap close.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (0390.HK, 601390.SS, CNYHKD=X); 52-week range 3.11-5.28 HKD
data_sources.financials: 0390.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics FY2017-FY2025, H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026); FY2025 annual report income statement and cash flow statement (pp.~120-127); H1 FY2026 interim report (share-change table, profit or loss, perpetual-note note)
data_sources.qualitative: 0390.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-11): FY2026 guidance, receivables/gearing disclosures, bull/bear cases

inputs.share_count_basis: Total A+H shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (20,323.92m A + 4,207.39m H), post cancellation of 135.7m buyback A-shares and 55.6m forfeited restricted shares (H1 FY2026 interim, share-change table). No material dilutive securities remain (2021 restricted-share scheme lapsed on missed KPIs). Held flat: buybacks (RMB160m FY2025, RMB640m H1 FY2026) are funded out of the distributable flow being valued.
inputs.net_debt_note: net_debt deliberately held at ZERO. The flow is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders, which is already after finance costs (RMB14.1bn FY2025), after the non-controlling interests' share (RMB3.5bn) and after perpetual-note distributions (~RMB1.96bn, the gap between attributable NI and basic EPS x shares). Deducting group net debt (H1 FY2026 borrowings RMB618.6bn less cash RMB153.8bn = RMB464.8bn), NCI (RMB169.5bn book) or perpetual notes (RMB55.4bn) as well would charge each claim twice. total_debt and cash are recorded for reference only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 cash dividends paid to owners of the Company (RMB6,418m, cash flow statement) -- the distributable flow actually paid, ~31% of earnings to ordinary shareholders (RMB20.9bn). Not reported_fcf - sbc - interest: that owner-FCF identity does not apply on this route.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF RMB28,772m less gross capex RMB60,286m (PP&E 16,901 + intangibles/PPP concessions 42,025 + lease prepayments 590 + investment properties 757 + mining 13). Negative in 7 of the last 9 years; cumulative FY2017-FY2025 = -RMB139.6bn.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, share-based payment line in the equity-settled reserve (RMB4m; FY2024 -RMB27m reversal). Immaterial -- SBC-zero market; explicit SBC rows kept at 0%, house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in RMB (CNY); H shares quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1721 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10T03:38Z; cross-check USD/HKD 7.8472 / USD/CNY 6.683 = 1.1742 (0.2% tie). Parity: A share 601390.SS RMB4.29 x 1.1721 = HK$5.03 vs H at HK$3.215 -- the H class trades at a ~36% discount to the A class (A/H premium ~56%), a persistent feature of CREC, so the parity check confirms rate direction but cannot tie the two lines. Per-share values are computed in RMB and converted; A and H rank pari passu economically, so the RMB value per share applies to both classes.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z HKEX regular close (Yahoo chart API); 52-week range 3.11-5.28 HKD; price sits ~3% above the 52-week low
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, RMB terms, because the flow is post-interest and accrues to ordinary equity: China 10y government bond ~1.8% + levered beta 1.25 x China ERP 7.0% = ~10.55%, rounded to 10.5%. The beta is above the ~1.0 typical of A-share SOE contractors because ordinary equity is a thin sliver (H-price market cap ~RMB67bn) on RMB465bn net debt, RMB170bn NCI and RMB55bn perpetuals -- the equity is a geared claim. SOE status cuts both ways (implicit state support lowers distress risk; SASAC objectives over shareholder returns) and is NOT given a separate premium; China sovereign/regulatory, local-government credit (receivables) and construction-cycle risk are carried in the bear flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked on the rate. Same 10.5% in every scenario (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases are inside the flow: attributable profit is after IFRS 16 depreciation and lease interest, and no lease liability is deducted (net_debt held at zero). Lease principal (RMB5.1bn FY2025) is a financing flow already absorbed in the payout-capacity haircut.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flow (profit to owners of the Company, less perpetual-note distributions); NCI is NOT deducted in the bridge. NCI book RMB169.5bn earns only RMB3.5bn (2%) and includes debt-like project-company capital from financial investors; valuing it at book would be both a double charge and an overstatement of the claim.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: the 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' row nominally sends CREC to owner-FCF + adaptations, but the skill's own trap list applies -- reported FCF is structurally negative (receivables funding for local-government owners, PPP/concession build-out), and an enterprise DCF here makes equity a ~10% residual of a ~RMB760bn claim stack (net debt 465 + NCI 170 + perps 55 + equity ~67). A 1pp change in normalised unlevered FCF margin (~RMB10bn/yr, ~RMB110bn of EV at 9% WACC) moves equity value by more than the entire market cap, and no defensible mid-cycle normalisation of a series that has been negative 7 of 9 years (cumulative -RMB140bn) gets enterprise FCF to the ~RMB55bn+/yr needed to cover the claims. That model is therefore not conservative, it is indeterminate. Instead the flow valued is what ordinary shareholders can actually be paid: earnings attributable to ordinary shareholders (post-interest, post-NCI, post-perpetual) times a PAYOUT-CAPACITY ratio, capitalised at cost of equity with net_debt = 0 (the REIT/AFFO engine pattern). Engine mapping: ebitda_margin_path = ordinary-shareholder NI margin; capex_pct_path = earnings that must be RETAINED (margin x (1 - payout capacity)) to fund receivables, contract assets and PPP equity at stable gearing; D&A, cash tax, SBC, working capital = 0 because they are already inside NI or inside the retention line. The retention line is the cash-conversion haircut: the company pays ~30% today and still borrows to fund the rest; steady-state clean-surplus retention at g=2% and ~6.6% ordinary ROE would be ~30%, so a 60% base payout capacity leaves a standing ~10pp allowance for receivable credit losses never booked through NI. ANCHORS: FY2025 ordinary NI RMB20.94bn (EPS 0.848 x weighted shares; 1.92% margin) vs mid-cycle FY2019-FY2024 2.3-2.6%; FY2026e ~RMB16.5bn (H1 7.9bn, H2 assumed -20% YoY on H1's -26.8% trend) on guided revenue RMB1,011.8bn = 1.63%. Workbook and JSON generated by make build-dcf.
inputs.fcf_normalization_note: Why not mid-cycle owner FCF: (1) PPP/concession intangible spend rose to RMB42.0bn in FY2025 despite the Nov-2023 'new PPP mechanism' that bans new government-pay PPP -- the existing pipeline is still being built, so the taper is a forecast, not an observation; (2) receivables +35% YoY to RMB485.9bn with turnover days 86->139 shows working capital consuming cash even while revenue shrinks -- the opposite of the release a shrinking contractor should show; (3) RMB102bn of receivables securitisation/factoring (RMB4.4bn derecognition losses) flatters OCF, so even the reported OCF overstates organic cash conversion. The payout-capacity ratio carries all three judgments in one auditable line per year.

bear.narrative: Local-government payment stress becomes credit loss: receivable impairments and property write-downs push ordinary NI margin to ~1.2%, revenue misses guidance and keeps falling into FY2029 as national construction output shrinks again, and payout capacity stays ~30% for three years (retained earnings keep disappearing into receivables) before reaching only 50%.

base.margin_note: ebitda_margin_path is ordinary-shareholder NI margin (post-interest, post-NCI, post-perpetual). FY2026 1.63% from H1 actual + H2 -20%; recovers to 2.0% by FY2030 as the anti-involution tender rules and lower admin/R&D (FY26 guided 'four expenses' RMB54.3bn vs ~59.7bn) offset property losses -- still below the 2.3-2.6% FY2019-FY2024 band because impairments and property drag do not fully clear.
base.capex_note: capex_pct_path is retained earnings required = margin x (1 - payout capacity). Payout capacity 32% FY2026 (today's ~31% actual) rising to 50% by FY2029 and 60% from FY2031, as PPP intangible spend tapers under the new PPP mechanism and the 2024-2028 local-government debt-swap programme pays down arrears.
base.narrative: Domestic construction volume troughs in FY2027-28 (guided revenue RMB1,011.8bn FY2026, new contracts flat at ~RMB2.75tn), then grows with nominal GDP on 15th Five-Year Plan rail/water/'Six Networks' spend and overseas work. Margins stabilise below the old band. Receivable growth stops but is not reversed; PPP spend tapers, so the share of earnings the group can pay out climbs from ~30% to 60%.

bull.narrative: Stimulus-backed rebound: ultra-long special treasury bonds and the debt swap clear local-government arrears, receivable days fall back toward ~100, overseas/BRI keeps growing double-digit, and copper/cobalt mining adds margin. NI margin returns to the bottom of the old 2.4% band; payout capacity reaches 70% (clean-surplus steady state) by FY2031 as PPP spend falls away.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 10x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% (house default 15%) because there is no sign of a bottom -- three years of decline, H1 FY2026 NI -26.8%, receivable days up 62% in one year and dependence on a single class of payer (local governments) whose finances are the core risk. Base 50%: guidance is explicit and the debt-swap programme is real money. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things at once (arrears cleared, margins restored, PPP spend falling) from an SOE whose priorities are set by SASAC.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
